1.  The pipeline will follow existing BC Gas RoW for approximately 75% of the route, and 109 of the 
total 137 water crossings will be on or immediately adjacent to existing BC Gas RoW;

2.  Twenty-one of the 28 new water crossings will be immediately adjacent to existing hydro 
transmission RoW, or on the CPR rail line through the Grand Forks area;

3.  Of the remaining 7 crossings; 
●     three are S6 streams with no fish potential, 
●     two are new crossing sites on the Kootenay River (main and old channel), but both will be 
directionally drilled, 
●     one is a very minor downstream realignment on the Kettle River that is proposed to allow a better 
crossing, 
●     one is a small fish-bearing stream (Cambridge Creek) that can be crossed using standard worksite 
isolation techniques (i.e., pump or flume),

BC Gas and the contractors will adhere to the requirements of the Forest Practices Code and all other applicable regional and municipal fire regulations. BC Gas will ensure that fire protection equipment and trained personnel are available on-site and will inform the respective fire authorities before construction activity takes place in their jurisdictions.

1. A possible historical cairn was noted in the vicinity of KP 51.3 on the Creston Mountain Divergence. Although it appears to be 
sufficiently distant that impact will not likely occur, it should be identified on all development and environmental management plans 
as an area to be avoided. Depending on the location of the final route, it may be necessary to protect this site with temporary fencing.

2. An abandoned and potentially historical railway bed may be used as a construction staging area for a portion of the 
Warfield/Rossland divergence. If this railway bed is utilised, it will be restored upon completion of construction.
Updating the estimate of BC Gas greenhouse gas emissions based on data for 1997 (the estimate in the January 1998 Application was based on 1996 data).

1. BC Gas must cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed, operated, dismantled and 
abandoned in accordance with the documents and commitments listed in Schedule A to this Certificate.

2. Subject to Condition 1, BC Gas must fulfil all commitments and proposed mitigation and 
compensation measures as documented in the Application, including commitments and measures 
contained in supplementary documents and correspondence listed in Schedule A to this Certificate, and 
must comply with all of the Conditions of this Certificate to the reasonable satisfaction of the Minister.

4. Despite Condition 1, if prior to receiving "Leave to Open" for the Pipeline, pursuant to the Pipeline 
Act (RSBC 1996, c.368), BC Gas proposes a change to the design, location, construction or operation of 
the Project as described in the documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate:
a) BC Gas must make application for such variation to authorities required to give approvals, licenses, 
permits or other authorizations under other enactments for implementation of the Project in accordance 
with that authority’s approval process unless:
i.  the variation would be subject to provisions of the Environmental Assessment Reviewable 
Projects Regulation (B.C. Reg. 276/95), if the Project was an existing facility; or
ii.  the variation, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister, is a modification:
●     to the proposed routing of the Pipeline right-of-way as set out in the documents listed in Schedule 
A to this Certificate;
●     to the techniques for crossing watercourses other than those proposed for each of the crossings as 
set out in the Environmental Protection Plan listed in Schedule A to this Certificate;
●     to the locations for crossing watercourses other than those set out in the documents listed in 
Schedule A to this Certificate;
●     to the location of the Hedley Compressor Station other than as proposed in the documents listed in 
Schedule A to this Certificate;
●     to the location for installation of two new compressor units at the Kitchener Compressor Station 
outside of the property currently owned by BC Gas for the Kitchener Compressor Station; or
●     that involves the construction or installation of facilities on or off the main site of the Project, 
which were not identified in the documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate.
b) For the changes listed in Condition 4 a)i and ii, BC Gas must, prior to receiving approvals, licenses, 
permits or other authorization under other enactments required for the variation to the Project, provide 
the Executive Director: 
i.  notice of the proposed change; and
ii.  plans, analyses, records and other information necessary for an effective assessment by the 
Executive Director of the proposed change.

6. If subsequent to the granting under the Pipeline Act of "Leave to Open", for the Pipeline, BC Gas 
requires a variation in the Project design, location, construction or operation as described in the 
documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate, BC Gas shall make application for such variation to 
authorities under other enactments for implementation of the Project in accordance with that authority’s 
approval process, unless the variation would be subject to the provisions of the Environmental 
Assessment Reviewable Projects Regulation.

7. Prior to upgrading or creating new access roads for the Pipeline right-of-way logging, BC Gas must complete a Noxious Weed and Weeds of Management Concern, Prevention and Control Plan to the reasonable satisfaction of the respective District Managers, Ministry of Forests; the Senior Habitat Biologist, MELP; and the District Agrologist, MAF.

7. Prior to upgrading or creating new access roads for the Pipeline right-of-way logging, BC Gas must complete an Access Management Plan to the reasonable satisfaction of the Senior Habitat Biologist, MELP; the respective District Managers, MoF; and the Regional Director, MoTH.

7. Prior to upgrading or creating new access roads for the Pipeline right-of-way logging, BC Gas must complete to the reasonable satisfaction of the Director, Archaeology Branch, any archaeological impact assessment studies that may be required for new or upgraded access roads in areas not previously subject to archaeological impact assessment, and implement any impact management measures deemed necessary.

8. Prior to logging of the Pipeline right-of-way, BC Gas must complete a Silviculture Plan to the reasonable satisfaction of the respective District Managers, MoF, and the Senior Habitat Biologist, MELP.

8. Prior to logging of the Pipeline right-of-way, BC Gas must complete a Forest Fire Prevention Plan to the reasonable satisfaction of the Forest Protection Officer, Southeast Fire Centre, Rock Creek.

8. Prior to logging of the Pipeline right-of-way, BC Gas must complete an Emergency Response Plan for the pre-construction phases of the Project to the reasonable satisfaction of the Regional Manager, Pollution Prevention, MELP, and the Manager, Emergency Preparedness Programs, Ministry of Health.
9. Prior to construction, BC Gas must complete a Water Quality Monitoring Program to the reasonable satisfaction of the Regional Manager, Pollution Prevention, MELP, and in consultation with DFO.

9. Prior to construction, BC Gas must complete an Erosion and Sediment Control Program to the reasonable satisfaction of the Regional Manager, Pollution Prevention, MELP, and in consultation with DFO.

9. Prior to construction, BC Gas must complete a Restoration Plan to the reasonable satisfaction of the Senior Habitat Biologist, MELP; the District Agrologist, MAF; and the respective District Managers, MoF.

9. Prior to construction, BC Gas must complete to the satisfaction of the Director, Archaeology Branch, any archaeological impact assessment studies required for new or upgraded access roads not previously assessed, and implement any impact management measures deemed necessary.

9. Prior to construction, BC Gas must complete an Emergency Response Plan for the construction phase to the reasonable satisfaction of the Regional Manager, Pollution Prevention, MELP, and the Manager, Environmental Preparedness Programs, Ministry of Health.

10. Prior to any clearing activities for the Project, BC Gas must complete a Terrestrial Wildlife Habitat Mitigation and Compensation Program to the reasonable satisfaction of the Senior Habitat Biologist, MELP, in consultation with MoF, the Canadian Wildlife Service, and the Creston Valley Wildlife Management Area board.

11. At the same time drafts of the plans and programs identified in Conditions 7-10 inclusive are provided to the respective agencies, BC Gas must provide copies to the Upper Similkameen Indian Band, the Lower Similkameen Indian Band, the Osoyoos Indian Band and the Lower Kootenay Band, for review and comment.

12. In the event the use of directional drilling is not found to be technically feasible at the crossing of the Columbia River, the main channel of the Kootenay River, or the channel of the Old Kootenay River, BC Gas must submit to DFO and MELP detailed plans regarding the contingency method to be used for the crossing.

13. BC Gas must, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister: 
a) have substantially started the Project, commencing its construction within five years of the issue date 
of this Certificate; and
b) have submitted to the EAO, within:
i.  two months of receiving "Leave to Open" the Pipeline, a report on compliance with the 
Conditions of this Certificate, and the schedule for submitting monitoring reports as required by 
the plans to be completed pursuant to Conditions 7-10 inclusive; and
ii.  twelve months of receiving "Leave to Open", statistics on construction jobs filled by local 
residents, for all phases of the Project.

During construction near the Dewdney Trail, BC Gas has committed: to work with the MoF, the Archaeology Branch and Okanagan Bands to ensure appropriate mitigation measures and procedures are followed; to concentrate new development in areas already disturbed; to ensure authorization of any unavoidable new disturbances under an Alteration Permit from MoF; and to return the trail to its existing condition after construction. BC Gas has also committed to engaging qualified archaeologists to apply for Heritage Investigation Permits under the HCA to complete additional studies for the six sites requiring mitigation.

• to the locations for crossing the watercourses other than those set out in the documents 
listed in Appendix A to this report;

Prior to Issuance of Project Approval Certificate: Completion of Environmental Protection Plan.
Prior to Issuance of Project Approval Certificate: File permit applications with the Archaeology Branch for heritage investigation and site alteration.

Prior to Upgrading of Access for Right-of-Way Logging: BC Gas will submit Access Management Plan(s) to MELP Regional Manager(s), FWH Program, and the Regional Manager, Water. Approvals will be sought from MoF and BCAL as required. The draft plan will be submitted to MELP Regional Biologists in Cranbrook and Penticton for review prior to initiating the first project-related disturbance.

Prior to Upgrading of Access for Right-of-Way Logging: BC Gas is committed to preparing a Noxious Weed Prevention and Control Plan acceptable to MELP and MoF, focused on species classified as noxious weeds provincially and within Regional Districts crossed by the SCP, finalising the list of weeds of management concern in consultation with MoF, MAFF, Osoyoos Indian Band and Regional Districts prior to land disturbance.
Crossing details will be provided in crossing approval applications as required by the Coast Guard for crossings of navigable waters, after the Project Approval Certificate has been granted.

Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: BC Gas will provide a notification to downstream water licencees, irrigation districts and/or placer miners for July Creek and Kettle River in accordance with the EAO's notification requirements.
Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: BC Gas is committed to continue to work with First Nations to assist them in achieving economic participation in the Project.
Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: BC Gas will conduct a noxious weed inventory at a 1:20 000 scale in accordance with weed mapping procedures to be outlined by the MoF.

Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: BC Gas is committed to reaching a satisfactory agreement with MELP on measurable and enforceable success/failure criteria for weed control in specified ecologically important zones; these criteria will be approved by MELP Regional staff prior to clearing or Project related land disturbance.
Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: Prepare an Emergency Response Plan.
Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: Prepare a Silviculture Plan.
Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: Prepare a Forest Fire Prevention Plan.

Prior to Right-of-Way Logging: BC Gas will mark wildlife trees in the field that have been selected for exclusion from felling before tree removal is undertaken, in compliance with Workers' Compensation Board safety standards. All field work will be done by qualified wildlife tree evaluators.
Prior to Pipeline Construction: BC Gas will prepare a list of field contacts for the Southern Crossing Pipeline Project.

Prior to Pipeline Construction: BC Gas is committed to continue to work with MELP Regional staff to define time exclusion intervals that can be practically met and which could reduce disturbance during sensitive times to wildlife such as nesting red and blue listed bird species, and snakes of special management interest in the South Okanagan Conservation Strategy area.
Prior to Pipeline Construction: BC Gas will contact and seek approval, as required, for HDD beneath dyke structures in the Creston area.

Prior to Pipeline Construction: BC Gas will continue to consult with MELP Regional Staff and MoF to define the geographic extent of ecologically important zones for identification in the SCP Restoration Plan.

Prior to Pipeline Construction: BC Gas is committed to consulting with both DFO and MELP staff to fine-tune fisheries work windows on a crossing-by-crossing basis to meet project scheduling requirements while mitigating impacts to acceptable levels.
Prior to Pipeline Construction: Complete archaeological investigation (monitoring of construction) of the Marshall property near Midway.
Prior to Pipeline Construction: Notification of property owners directly affected by construction.
Prior to Pipeline Construction: Undertake archaeological investigation (inspection) of three areas prior to final decision on pipeline routing.
Notification to the Ministry of Health prior to construction in community watersheds.

During Construction: BC Gas will ensure that blasting conducted in or about fish-bearing waters will be in compliance with DFO's 1998 document Guidelines for the Use of Explosives in or near Canadian Fisheries Waters.

During Construction: BC Gas will avoid the destruction of migratory bird nests to the extent practical, and will schedule clearing and construction activities so as to avoid the nesting season of migratory birds as much as practical in sensitive areas along the pipeline route such as the CVWMA.

During Construction: BC Gas will have an archaeological monitor present when trench excavation is undertaken at Creston Flats (approx. KP 40.0 to KP 45.0) and during initial development activity in the Midway divergence section that could not be examined due to landowner concerns. If archaeological sites are located, all ground disturbing activity would cease until a qualified archaeological consultant conducts a site and impact assessment under a heritage inspection permit; if systematic data recovery is recommended, activity is delayed until a heritage investigation permit is obtained and mitigation is completed.
During Restoration: The Environmental Assessment Application commits BC Gas to minimizing impacts on the Dewdney Trail, and replacing the trail tread when construction is completed.

During Restoration: As a minimum, BC Gas will restore all Provincial Crown lands to a level satisfactory to the MoF under the FPC, and will endeavour to restore natural habitats to the extent practical on sensitive land that is not Provincial Crown Land; private landowner and Federal Government restoration requirements will be accommodated.
